question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{x+6}+\frac{1}{x+8})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{x+6}+\frac{1}{x+8})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x+6}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+8}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+6|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+8|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+6)(x+8)|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(x+6)(x+8)|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

domain.K: positive arbitrary separately on each real connected component
